title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
technique: reuse precomputed per-chunk KV caches for non-prefix RAG contexts and selectively recompute ~15% of tokens (those with highest KV deviation) to restore cross-chunk attention; loading/recompute pipelined, storage device chosen to hide delay

optimized_metrics.evidence: To speed up the prefill of the long LLM inputs, one can pre-compute the KV cache of a text and re-use the KV cache when the context is reused as the prefix of another LLM input.
Goal. When an LLM input includes multiple re-used text chunks, how to quickly combine their precomputed KV caches in order to achieve the same generation quality as the expensive full prefill
optimized_metrics.locator: §3 (goal) / abstract 'without compromising generation quality'; quality loss budget <=0.015 F1 in §7.3

headline_claim.text: CacheBlend reduces time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 2.2-3.3x and increases the inference throughput by 2.8-5x from full KV recompute without compromising generation quality.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 14 (TTFT vs average request rate per second)
storage-device choice (cheapest device with no extra delay), §5

metric_definitions.definition_quote: before generating any token, an LLM first uses prefill to go through the entire LLM input to produce the KV cache ... Thus, the prefill delay determines the time to first token (TTFT).
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT treated as prefill delay incl. KV loading from storage and selective recompute; Fig 12 reports the average over requests.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: CacheBlend achieves lower delay with higher throughput by 2.8-5x than all the baselines across different models and datasets.
metric_definitions.notes: Never defined formally; operationalised as the sustainable request rate at a given (similar) TTFT, i.e. req/s, read from the TTFT-vs-request-rate curve. Abstract: 'At the same TTFT, CacheBlend can increase throughput by up to 5x'.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: F1-score [6] is used to evaluate 2WikiMQA and Musique datasets ... Rouge-L score [39] is used to evaluate MultiNews and SAMSum datasets [12]. It measures the similarity between the model's ...
metric_definitions.notes: Quality is a hard constraint: 'reduction in F1 and Rouge-L score is within 0.02'.

load_regime: request-rate sweep (average request rate per second) on RAG queries; storage initially empty (first 1K queries skipped)
tradeoff_acknowledged: Full KV reuse is fastest (lowest TTFT) but quality drops sharply (often >2x); CacheBlend pays small extra recompute (5-18% of tokens) and <=0.02 F1/Rouge-L loss; MapRerank slightly lower TTFT but much worse quality.
hardware: 2x NVIDIA A40, 128GB RAM-class host, 1TB NVMe SSD (4.8 GB/s)
workloads: 2WikiMQA, Musique (and extended), SAMSum, MultiNews; RAG chunks of 512 tokens, top-6 chunks
extractor_notes: Throughput is never defined; it is request rate in the TTFT-vs-rate plot (average TTFT, no tail). Quality-vs-latency Pareto is explicit: the system picks the recompute ratio r* (~15%) that hides loading delay with negligible quality drop.
load_class_quote: Figure 12 compares the average quality and TTFT across the requests (no load); Figure 14: Average Request Rate per Second (request-rate sweep)
